description: A district curriculum director must authorize a student oral-history project and finalize its participant scope, supervision, recording safeguards, public-exhibit rules, and family consent process, with input from a classroom teacher, privacy officer, librarian, and family liaison.

shared_context.S1: The district is preparing a student oral-history project for the spring term, ending with a public school exhibit.
shared_context.S2: The current draft proposes participation by students in grades 7 and 8, one supervising adult per session, cloud-based audio storage, a 90-day retention period, and a public exhibit of selected recordings.
shared_context.S3: Dr. Chen has final authority to approve the project design and its implementation records.
shared_context.S4: The district's routine project-review meeting includes the classroom teacher, privacy officer, librarian, and family liaison before Dr. Chen signs off on the plan.

PF1.text: Mr. Romero's classroom pilot showed that the project is instructionally ready only for grade 8, and each interview session requires exactly two supervising adults because students work with recording equipment and community guests; he recorded these findings in his end-of-pilot notes, but the draft plan still contains the original scope and staffing.

PF2.text: The district privacy review requires recordings to remain on the district's encrypted internal server, be deleted exactly 45 days after the exhibit closes, and require signed guardian consent before any student records an interview; Ms. Shah completed the review, but the draft still uses the preliminary cloud-storage language.

PF3.text: The archive and rights review permits each public exhibit audio excerpt to be no longer than exactly 3 minutes and requires contributor attribution beside every excerpt; Ms. Brooks completed the rights check, but its limits have not been added to the exhibit template.

PF4.text: Family outreach confirmed that consent materials must be available in exactly English, Spanish, and Arabic, and that paper consent forms must be offered in addition to the online form; Mr. Okafor completed the outreach review, but the family-materials checklist has not been revised.

acceptance_conditions: The project must be limited to grade 8.
Each interview session must have exactly two supervising adults.
Recordings must be stored on the district encrypted internal server.
Recordings must be deleted exactly 45 days after the exhibit closes.
Signed guardian consent must be required before recording.
Each public audio excerpt must be limited to exactly 3 minutes.
Every public excerpt must include contributor attribution.
Consent materials must be available in exactly English, Spanish, and Arabic.
Paper consent forms must be available.
The approved plan must include a formal implementation or revision commitment.
The privacy review must be cited in the decision justification after being stated by the privacy officer.

content_checks.C10: any(c['type'] in ['revision', 'follow-up', 'plan_revision', 'privacy_compliance', 'document_update', 'document_revision', 'update_draft', 'update_exhibit_template', 'update_family_materials_checklist', 'materials_revision', 'exhibit_template_update', 'privacy_implementation', 'family_consent_access', 'review_followup'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The teacher's pilot changes the participant scope from grades 7 and 8 to grade 8 only and changes supervision from one adult to exactly two adults per session.

The privacy review changes storage to the district encrypted internal server, retention to exactly 45 days, and recording access to signed guardian consent, while requiring an implementation or revision commitment.
The rights review changes the public exhibit rule to a maximum excerpt of exactly 3 minutes and requires contributor attribution for every excerpt.
Family outreach changes the consent materials to exactly English, Spanish, and Arabic and adds paper consent availability plus an implementation or revision commitment.
